When a light ray passes through the rectangular glass block as shown,

sin psin q=sin ssin r= ng

tb-3A02-4.question:
(For Q4–5.) A ray of light travels from air to media P, Q and R in turn. Different sets of angles of incidence i and the corresponding angles of refraction r are measured. Figure c shows the graphs of sin i against sin r for the three media.

Which of the following statements is/are correct?

(2) R is optically denser than Q.

(3) Light travels slower in R than in P.

B (3) only

Slope of the graph =sinisinr= n

From the graph, nP > nQ > nR.

∴ (1) is correct. (2) is incorrect

A ray of light travels as shown (Fig e).

In which of the following cases may total internal reflection occur?

(1) Light travels from R to P.

(2) Light travels from Q to S.

B (1) and (3) only

tb-3A02-8.question:
A diver is looking at the air-water interface, of which the critical angle is C (Fig f).

The diver cannot see objects in region

A P.

B Q.

C R.

D S.
tb-3A02-8.reasoning:
Light rays from regions P and Q can reach the diver by refracting at the air-water interface.

Light rays from region R can reach the diver by total internal reflection at the air-water interface.

For light rays from region S, only a small proportion of rays is reflected to the diver as the angle of incidence at the air-water interface is smaller than the critical angle. Therefore, the diver can hardly see objects in region S.

tb-3A02-9.question:
Figure g shows a light ray entering a spherical water droplet from air at point P and reaches point Q. O is the centre of the droplet. The refractive index of water is n.

Which of the following are correct?

(1) sin i = n sin r

(2) Total internal reflection will never occur at point P.

(3) Total internal reflection will never occur at point Q.

A (1) and (2) only

B (1) and (3) only

C (2) and (3) only

D (1), (2) and (3)
tb-3A02-9.reasoning:
By n1 sin θ1 = n2 sin θ2,

1 sin i = n sin r

∴ (1) is correct.

Total internal reflection will never occur when light travels from an optical less dense medium to an optically denser medium.

∴ (2) is correct.

As the water droplet is spherical, by symmetry, the angle of incidence at Q equals the angle of refraction at P, which is always smaller than the critical angle.

∴ (3) is correct.

tb-3A02-10.question:
Figure h shows a straight optical fibre. The refractive indices of the core and the cladding are n1 and n2 respectively, and n1 > n2.

For a ray of light passing from one end of the fibre to the other end without leaking from the core, if the minimum time needed is T, what is the maximum time needed?

A Tn1

B Tn2

C n1n2T

D n2n1T
tb-3A02-10.reasoning:
The time taken is minimum if the light ray travels in a straight line.

Distance travelled D = vt =cn1T

Let C be the critical angle at the core-cladding interface.

sin C =n2n1

The time taken is maximum if the light ray travels in a path that hits the interface at angle C.

Total distance travelled =DsinC=1sin C(cn1T)

Maximum time needed =1sin C(cn1T)cn1

=n1n2T

tb-3A02-11.question:
Two coloured lights P and Q strike medium X at the same point from a vacuum and then travel in medium X along the same path as shown (Fig i). Which of the following statements is/are correct?

(1) Dispersion occurs.

(2) P and Q travel with the same speed in X.

(3) The refractive index for P in X is smaller than that for Q.

A (1) only

B (3) only

C (1) and (2) only

D (2) and (3) only
tb-3A02-11.reasoning:
Dispersion occurs when white light undergoes refraction and spreads into different colours.

∴ (1) is incorrect.

By n1 sin θ1 = n2 sin θ2, as rays P and Q have the same angle of refraction but different angles of incidence, they have different refractive indices and therefore different speeds in X.

∴ (2) is incorrect.

Ray P deflects less than ray Q. Therefore, the refractive index for P in X is smaller than that for Q.

∴ (3) is correct.
